stories.headline: Over 100,000 join new Yellow Vest protests in France
body: About 106,000 people marched across France in new cost-of-living protests, the government said.
Turnout fell from 146,000 the week before, and the protests stayed mostly calm.
Student unions put the number at 200,000.
stories.vc: Ongoing protests keep pressure on France to raise wages and cut costs.

stories.headline: Fuel crisis and protests hit Chile's far-right president
body: Chile's President José Antonio Kast's approval has fallen to 24% after eight months in power.
A fuel crisis and student protests over living costs are piling pressure on him.
Students are also angry over reduced sentences for some sex offenders.
stories.vc: Political instability can unsettle investors in Chile's copper and lithium industries.

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first three-way meeting at APEC
body: Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will meet together for the first time at APEC in Shenzhen, China.
The summit runs on 18-19 November.
Talks will focus on nuclear weapons, the White House says; the Iran war is also expected to come up.
stories.joke: Three leaders, one table, many egos.
stories.vc: Any thaw between the big powers could ease trade tensions and lift global markets.

stories.headline: Indian startup stocks add about $8B this week
body: 55 of 69 listed new-age tech stocks rose this week, Inc42 data shows.
Their combined value rose 4.5% to $177 billion.
E2E Networks, Turtlemint and PB Fintech led; Meesho, Paytm and Groww hit new highs.
stories.joke: Startup stocks are on a winning streak. Don't jinx it.
stories.vc: A strong market for listed startups supports Razorpay's and others' IPO plans.

stories.headline: Coal India's Mahanadi Coalfields files for a ₹9,500 crore IPO
body: Mahanadi Coalfields, a Coal India subsidiary, filed its prospectus for an IPO.
Coal India will sell up to 10% of its stake.
The issue could raise about ₹9,500 crore.
stories.joke: Coal goes public: a hot listing, literally.
stories.vc: Big PSU listings bring fresh supply for investors and cash for the government.

stories.headline: India opens registration for data 'consent managers'
body: MeitY has opened registration for consent managers under India's data protection law.
These firms will help people control how their personal data is used.
The next phase of the law takes effect in May 2027.
stories.joke: Finally, someone to ask permission for you.
stories.vc: A new regulated industry for consent management opens up for startups.

stories.headline: Musk and others petition Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang
body: A petition asking Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang has over 115,000 signatures, including about 6,000 Nvidia staff.
Elon Musk, Replit's Amjad Masad and Epic's Tim Sweeney signed it.
Signers say Huang was removed without proper process.
stories.vc: Pressure from employees and shareholders adds to uncertainty over Nvidia's leadership.

stories.headline: Tesla opens Cybercab pre-orders for personal use
body: Tesla opened pre-orders for its self-driving Cybercab to select customers, priced at $29,990.
Owners must also pay $299 a month to run it.
It will work only in certain areas of a few Texas cities at first.
stories.joke: A car you own but pay monthly to drive you. Progress.
stories.vc: Subscription fees could become Tesla's new steady income stream.

stories.headline: The AI graveyard: projects and startups that didn't make it
body: About 42% of company AI projects are abandoned, S&P Global says.
Chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy last month.
Reasons include funding gaps, tech problems and weak demand.
stories.joke: Even AI has a 'none of the above' option.
stories.vc: High failure rates are a warning for investors pricing AI as a sure thing.

stories.headline: Analysis: Anthropic's huge valuation can't guarantee its edge
body: Anthropic plans an IPO valuing it at up to $1.4 trillion.
Its market value on outstanding shares may be nearer $1 trillion.
The analysis warns a giant valuation doesn't secure its lead over rivals.
stories.joke: A trillion-dollar moat still needs water.
stories.vc: IPO buyers must decide if AI leaders can defend their lead over time.

stories.headline: Copper hits near four-month low on rate and AI demand fears
body: Copper fell about 1.8% to $13,462 a tonne, near a four-month low.
Traders expect higher US interest rates and weaker demand from China and tech.
Prices had eased since the US midterms.
stories.vc: Copper is a gauge for the AI and power build-out; a slide hints at slowing demand.

stories.headline: Karnataka launches a menopause health programme for women
body: Karnataka will pilot 'Ruthu Taare', a mid-life women's health and menopause programme, in Dakshina Kannada.
It covers women aged 35 and above.
Actor and former MP Ramya is the brand ambassador.
stories.vc: Menopause care is a fast-growing women's health market that public programmes can help unlock.

stories.headline: Malda Medical College orders no woman in labour be turned away at night
body: Malda Medical College says no pregnant woman with labour pain can be denied admission at night.
They must get care and a bed even if birth is not close.
The order follows criticism over a recent childbirth incident.
stories.vc: Safer maternity care in public hospitals lowers costly emergencies later.

stories.headline: Kerala doctor arrested over alleged assault attempt on junior woman doctor
body: A senior doctor at Nedumangad District Hospital was arrested for allegedly trying to sexually assault a junior woman doctor.
She escaped and told colleagues, who helped her go to police.
She was doing her house surgery training.
stories.vc: Safe workplaces are key to keeping women in medicine.

stories.headline: Delhi's MCD to open dialysis centres at 7 hospitals
body: Delhi's MCD will set up dialysis centres at seven of its hospitals under a public-private partnership.
Treatment will cost less than at private hospitals.
Ayushman Bharat beneficiaries will get it cashless.
stories.vc: PPP dialysis units expand kidney care fast without big public capital spending.

stories.headline: 178 more specialist seats added in NEET PG round 2
body: The Medical Counselling Committee added 178 postgraduate medical seats to round 2 of NEET PG counselling.
It also removed 6 seats.
The changes came from updates sent by medical institutes.
stories.vc: More specialist seats mean more doctors for hospitals in coming years.

stories.headline: Kerala wants Karnataka-registered doctors to work in Kasaragod
body: Kerala has recommended letting Karnataka-registered doctors practise in Kasaragod district.
The district faces a shortage of medical staff.
Kerala also wants more doctors, nurses and technicians for its hospitals there.
stories.vc: Cross-state staffing could quickly fill gaps in border-area hospitals.

stories.headline: McLaren brings upgrades to Las Vegas, its toughest track
body: McLaren will bring upgrades to its MCL40 for the Las Vegas GP.
The team calls them the foundation for next year's car.
It comes after Norris won from pole in Brazil.
stories.joke: Fixing your worst track with next year's parts: bold.
stories.vc: Early development for 2027 could pay off in prize money next season.
